messages:
pranav: quick question for the batcher folks — i'm sketching an RFC for per-tenant soft buffering (small reserved window) vs keeping a single global credit pool. looking for practical tradeoffs we might've seen in prod.
jen: tl;dr: per-tenant gives predictable tail isolation, global pool gives better steady-state throughput.
alex: +1. with per-tenant we avoid noisy neighbors, but you risk underutilization unless you allow borrowing.
maria: borrowing is the hard part. if you do permissive borrow you need strong guardrails so one tenant doesn't starve the reserve when traffic spikes.
pranav: right. current thought: reserve X tokens per tenant as "soft" (can be preempted), plus a global opportunistic pool. preemption should be non-blocking.
tina: what does non-blocking preemption mean here? do you force-evict inflight microbatches? that sounds risky for latency SLOs.
pranav: not force-evict. more like prevent new allocations into the tenant reserve and kick their queued-but-not-started requests onto opportunistic pool; in-flight stays.
sam: that's reasonable. avoids tearing KV cache and keeps tail predictable. but you need an admission fastpath so small requests don't get trapped behind big ones.
jen: observability note: track "borrowed_from_reserve" metric per tenant + event when borrow > threshold. that lets SRE set alerts/auto-throttle.
alex: another angle: instead of token counts, use windowed headroom meters (ms of expected gpu time). simpler to reason about for latency.
maria: we tried a headroom-meter prototype last quarter. it matched latency better but was more sensitive to model length variance — harder to tune across tenants.
pranav: hmm. what about hybrid: per-tenant soft token reserve + headroom scoring to prioritize opportunistic pool? so reserve gives isolation, headroom orders the spare capacity.
tina: love that. also add a backoff hint in the response header so SDKs can backpressure nicely when they hit borrowing frequently. small UX win.
sam: +1. implement borrow_allowed flag on the enqueue API and emit a reason code like BORROW_OK / BORROW_DENIED / INSUFFICIENT_HEADROOM.
jen: security/ops: ensure audit log when borrow crosses threshold or when borrow was forcibly denied. enterprise teams will want to see that.
pranav: noted. last question: eviction semantics — soft reserve eviction should be prioritized by least-recently-started queued requests, not by size. otherwise big low-prio requests could unblock the pool while tiny latency-critical ones wait.
alex: agree. LR-started queued ordering (or a priority score) is best. and we should include an experiment flag to flip to size-based in case a customer workload prefers throughput.
maria: small UX nit: include a tenant-visible metric for "effective reserve utilization" so customers can tune their config. many will misinterpret raw tokens.
ci-bot: build status: batcher-sim-tests passed on branch per-tenant-reserve-hybrid (12/12).
pranav: thanks team — i'll fold this into the RFC draft. will add a short runbook for when borrow spikes and a couple of simulation graphs. ping me if you want to add testcases. :thumbsup:
